doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Algiers halls and the picnic boat
title: Edmund Payton, Ruben Manuel's brass band and Harry's Yard
summary: Martin and Tom name older Algiers bands: Edmund Payton on bass, banjo and guitar, a second Payton on Franklin Street, and Ruben Manuel's brass band playing under a tree in old Harry's yard. Martin remembers sitting on Harry's black horse as a boy.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: That's right. And along that time, you take, Luriat was running, that's what the white place up there at the naval station, they were playing there. They had bands up there, you played there too Tom? Yeah, I played there. Yeah, Peter and Peter. But now before you had Peter and then you had my father-in-law there, Edmund Payton. Edmund Payton. Edmund Payton. So what did Payton play? He played bass and banjo, guitar.
Seems like I once heard something about Payton had an accordion band or something. Did he ever play accordion or did he have any?
Yeah, Payton used to play over here. That's on Franklin Street, we called it Franklin Street. That was a different Payton. Yes, a different Payton. Different Payton.

Now, before you timed there, right along, it was old, the band was there in that section. That was old man. Dorsey? No, no, Dorsey was up further. They take Ruben Manuel and them was down in there. Ruben Manuel, you remember old man Ruben Manuel?
Yeah, that's why they had the brass band.

Yeah. Ruben Manuel and Harry, he used to play drum in there man. Under that tree. Under that tree. Right down there under that tree. Jill Davis. Jill, but now them people be hundred after they be there.

Sure would. I remember Manuel Mineta showed us a big tree not far from his house over there on Leboeuf Street where they had picnics when he was a boy. Would it be near there? That's full of them. Up near these railroad tracks and all, not far from that.
You're talking about Whitney Avenue, that big old oak tree.
Yeah, it was up there near Whitney.
That big old oak tree. That's that.
This was a different tree you were talking about.

Yeah, yeah, this tree was down in old Harry's Yard. You used to come down there when I was a kid and play. Oh yeah, I played down in Harry's Yard. I was a kid, used to play down there. Yeah. You see, Harry had that black horse and used to set me up on the horse while they all played music.
That's been good a long time.
